title: Stats With LLMs: Expert in the Loop
intro: LLMs remove the software friction from statistics: upload a CSV, describe the comparison, and the model writes and runs the code. The calculation is deterministic; the choices around it aren't.

topics.title: Stats With LLMs: Expert in the Loop

learn.title: Pick the test from the question
learn.text:
**Two independent groups, numeric** → two-sample t-test (paired if the same people did both)
**Three or more groups, or several factors** → ANOVA, then follow-up comparisons
**Categories vs categories** → chi-squared test of association (version × completed yes/no)
**Ranking options** → pairwise methods (Schulze, Borda tie-break), not averages
**Two numeric measures together** → correlation or regression — association, not cause

try.q: You compare completion (yes/no) across two design versions. Which test?

learn.title: Same people, or different people?
learn.text:
The t-test has two forms, and picking the wrong one is a common error.

**Two-sample** — different people in each group.
**Paired** — the same people did both, so each person is their own control.

With three or more groups you move to ANOVA; a significant ANOVA only says *something* differs, so follow-up comparisons tell you which groups.

try.q: The same twelve participants tried both versions. Which test?
try.explain: Each person acts as their own control.

learn.title: Expert in the loop
learn.text:
The workflow: you describe the analysis including the design, the model writes and runs the code, you check the data preparation and interpret the result against the decision.

The calculation is deterministic. The judgement isn't.

*Calabro's 2023–24 tutorials did all this in Minitab, SPSS, Excel and R. The method choice hasn't changed; the tooling has.*

try.q: What hasn't changed since the Minitab and SPSS tutorials?
try.explain: The tooling changed; the method choice didn't.

test.q: Which part of the work is deterministic?
What should you use to aggregate rankings?
test.explain: Schulze or Borda; averaging ranks is the classic mistake.

test.q: A significant ANOVA across four groups tells you what?
test.explain: Follow-up comparisons identify which groups differ.

test.q: What must the researcher check about the model's work?
test.explain: A correct calculation on wrongly prepared data is still wrong.

test.q: When is a correlation or regression the right choice?
test.explain: And it shows association, not cause.
